subQuestions.questionText: Choose the term/concept in COLUMN B that completes the statement: '… refers to the location of a rural settlement in relation to the surrounding environment.' (Y: Site / Z: Situation)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Z (Situation) (1 mark)
Situation refers to the location of a rural settlement in relation to its surrounding environment, while site refers to the actual ground on which the settlement is built.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose the term/concept in COLUMN B that completes the statement: '… settlements locate in areas where the water supply is scarce.' (Y: Wet-point / Z: Dry-point)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Z (Dry-point) (1 mark)
Dry-point settlements locate in areas where water supply is scarce or where they are away from water (to avoid flooding), while wet-point settlements locate where water is readily available.

subQuestions.questionText: The sketch illustrates a … rural settlement pattern (refer to sketch in question paper showing clustered farmsteads with roads). (Y: nucleated / Z: dispersed)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Y (nucleated) (1 mark)
The sketch shows farmsteads clustered closely together, which is the defining feature of a nucleated rural settlement pattern.

subQuestions.questionText: An advantage generally associated with a dispersed rural settlement pattern is … (Y: greater safety / Z: larger profits)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Z (larger profits) (1 mark)
Dispersed settlements involve farmsteads spread far apart on large landholdings, allowing for extensive commercial farming and larger profits. Greater safety is typically associated with nucleated settlements.

subQuestions.questionText: A … settlement is dominated by primary activities. (Y: rural / Z: urban)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Y (rural) (1 mark)
Rural settlements are dominated by primary activities such as farming, fishing, mining and forestry. Urban settlements are dominated by secondary and tertiary activities.

subQuestions.questionText: The shape of the settlement in the sketch is … (refer to sketch showing farmsteads aligned along a river). (Y: semi-circular / Z: linear)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Z (linear) (1 mark)
The settlement is arranged in a line along the river, which is the defining feature of a linear settlement shape.

subQuestions.questionText: A circular shaped settlement can be influenced by a … (Y: water point / Z: river)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Y (water point) (1 mark)
A circular settlement forms around a central feature such as a water point (e.g. a borehole or well), with farmsteads arranged in a circle around it. Rivers typically produce linear settlements.

subQuestions.questionText: … farming occurs when agriculture is practised extensively. (Y: Large-scale / Z: Small-scale)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Y (Large-scale) (1 mark)
Large-scale (extensive) farming uses large areas of land with relatively low inputs per unit area, typical of commercial agriculture. Small-scale farming is intensive and uses small plots.

subQuestions.questionText: The … street pattern is commonly found in the central business district of old cities.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (grid-iron) (1 mark)
Grid-iron (or rectangular) street patterns, with streets intersecting at right angles, are commonly found in the CBDs of old planned cities.

subQuestions.questionText: Traffic congestion is associated with the … street pattern where roads converge at the city centre.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (radial) (1 mark)
In a radial street pattern, roads converge at a central point (the city centre), which causes heavy traffic congestion at the centre.

subQuestions.questionText: A characteristic of street pattern P is that streets … (refer to sketch P showing streets intersecting at right angles).
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (intersect at right angles) (1 mark)
Street pattern P is a grid-iron pattern, characterised by streets intersecting at right angles to form rectangular blocks.

subQuestions.questionText: The street pattern R is characterised by … (refer to sketch R showing concentric circles with radial roads).
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (circular roads) (1 mark)
Street pattern R is a radial-concentric pattern, characterised by circular (concentric) roads around a central point connected by radial roads.

subQuestions.questionText: The advantages of street pattern Q are: (i) Easy to plan (ii) Smooth flow of traffic (iii) Saves fuel (iv) Regular-shaped plots (refer to sketch Q showing irregular street pattern).
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B ((ii) and (iii)) (1 mark)
Street pattern Q is an irregular pattern. Its advantages are smooth flow of traffic (fewer intersections so traffic flows freely) and fuel saving (vehicles do not have to stop frequently). It is not easy to plan and does not produce regular-shaped plots.

subQuestions.questionText: The profile in the sketch is a … view of a city. (refer to sketch showing buildings of different heights with the CBD labelled)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (side) (1 mark)
An urban profile is a side (cross-sectional) view of a city showing the relative heights of buildings across the urban area.

subQuestions.questionText: TWO characteristics of the urban profile in the sketch: (i) Tallest buildings in the CBD (ii) Lowest building density in the CBD (iii) Highest building density in the CBD (iv) Tallest buildings on the outskirts.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B ((i) and (iii)) (1 mark)
The sketch shows that the CBD has both the tallest buildings (because of high land values driving vertical growth) and the highest building density (buildings packed closely together).

subQuestions.questionText: Quote evidence from the extract to show that there has been progress with land reform.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: 'The progress made is better than what politicians claim' (1 mark)
Award 1 mark for a direct quote from the extract that indicates progress with land reform.

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the diagram and name the programme of land reform which has resulted in 6,68 million hectares of land being returned to the rightful owners.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: Land restitution (1 mark)
Land restitution is the programme that returns land to the rightful owners (those dispossessed under apartheid laws), which according to the diagram amounts to 6,68 million hectares.

subQuestions.questionText: According to the extract, name the economic principle that has been used for land redistribution in South Africa.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: Willing-buyer-willing-seller (1 mark)
The extract states that the government applied a market-assisted economic principle of land redistribution based on the willing-buyer-willing-seller principle.

- Seller reluctant to sell their land (accept examples) (2)
- Corruption with regards to the process (accept examples) (2)

- Cultural values will hamper land exchange (accept examples) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: … is when a country has sufficient and nutritious food that is accessible to all its people.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (Food security) (1 mark)
Food security is defined as a country having sufficient and nutritious food that is accessible to all its people.

subQuestions.questionText: A negative economic factor affecting production of food in a country is …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (a lack of capital) (1 mark)
A lack of capital is an economic factor that limits food production. Pests, diseases, droughts and floods are physical/environmental factors, while technology and mechanisation are positive factors.

subQuestions.questionText: An advantage of planting genetically modified crops to improve food security is …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (greater resistance to pests and diseases) (1 mark)
GM crops are engineered to be more resistant to pests and diseases, which is a key advantage for food security. The other options describe disadvantages or are incorrect.

options.A: that seeds can be recycled from new crops.
options.B: greater resistance to pests and diseases.
options.D: that farmers have easy access to seeds.

subQuestions.questionText: A social advantage of food-secure countries is that they …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (have reduced poverty) (1 mark)
Reduced poverty is a social advantage of food security. Importing/exporting food are economic considerations, and increased poverty is a disadvantage.

subQuestions.questionText: The province with the highest percentage of food insecurity in South Africa is … (Refer to the pie graph on food insecurity per province in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (Limpopo) (1 mark)
According to the pie graph, Limpopo has the highest food insecurity percentage at 25%.

subQuestions.questionText: Gauteng has a low percentage of food insecurity because of increased production from … farmers and a higher … rate. (i) subsistence (ii) large-scale (iii) employment (iv) crime
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C ((ii) and (iii)) (1 mark)
Gauteng's low food insecurity is due to large-scale (commercial) farming production and a higher employment rate which gives people purchasing power to buy food.

subQuestions.questionText: Provinces where the core industrial regions are located account for … of the food insecurity in South Africa.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (45%) (1 mark)
According to the official memo, the correct answer is B (45%), reflecting the combined food insecurity percentage in those provinces hosting the core industrial regions of South Africa.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the statement with ONE of the types of industries: 'Associated with less pollution and is usually not capital intensive.' (Options: break-of-bulk industry; footloose industry; light industry; market-orientated industry; raw material orientated; heavy industry; ubiquitous industry)
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: Light (industry) (1 mark)
Light industries produce small consumer goods, are associated with less pollution and are not capital intensive.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the statement with ONE of the types of industries: 'Located close to the customer as goods are perishable.'
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: Market orientated (industry) (1 mark)
Market-orientated industries locate close to the customer/market because their goods are perishable, fragile, or gain weight/bulk during production.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the statement with ONE of the types of industries: 'May be located anywhere and is widely distributed.'
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: Ubiquitous (industry) (1 mark)
Ubiquitous industries can be located anywhere and are widely distributed because their raw materials and markets are found everywhere (e.g. bakeries, brick-making).

subQuestions.questionText: Match the statement with ONE of the types of industries: 'Associated with high levels of pollution and occupy large spaces.'
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: Heavy (industry) (1 mark)
Heavy industries (e.g. iron and steel) are associated with high pollution levels and require large spaces for operations.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the statement with ONE of the types of industries: 'Located close to raw materials that are bulky.'
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: Raw material orientated (industry) (1 mark)
Raw material orientated industries locate near bulky/heavy/perishable raw materials to reduce transport costs (e.g. iron and steel, sugar refining).

subQuestions.questionText: Match the statement with ONE of the types of industries: 'Location is not determined by raw materials or markets.'
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: Footloose (industry) (1 mark)
Footloose industries are not tied to either raw materials or markets and can locate anywhere (e.g. high-tech, electronics).

subQuestions.questionText: Match the statement with ONE of the types of industries: 'Located where goods are transferred from one mode of transport to another.'
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: Break-of-bulk-point (industry) (1 mark)
Break-of-bulk-point industries are located at points where goods change from one mode of transport to another (e.g. harbours, where ships transfer cargo to rail or road).

subQuestions.questionText: Match the statement with ONE of the types of industries: 'Shoe manufacturing is an example of this type of industry.'
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: Light (industry) (1 mark)
Shoe manufacturing is a typical example of a light industry, producing small consumer goods with limited pollution and lower capital requirements.
